name: rail-tie-and-connectivity
prompt: This BGA brings ground out on two repeated-name rails (GND, RSVDGND) and its core supply on VCCINT plus a single VCCAUX pin. Tie both ground rails to one net and the core balls plus VCCAUX to another, then write tests that prove the ties actually held. I have no runtime available, so the tests must run offline.

inputs.notes: A wide repeated-name rail is the first thing written against a large part, and it is where the net API's shape bites: Net(...) takes an iterable, += takes a port or a Net and never a bare list. The reference part is a stand-in with 24 GND, 6 RSVDGND and 8 VCCINT ports — the shape of the tie is what is under test, not the part.
inputs.environment: Offline. jitx.test.TestCase activates the instantiation context with no runtime and no parts database, so nothing here needs auth or a network.

expected_output: A Circuit that ties both ground rails in one Net(...) call and the core rail plus the scalar pin into a second net, with a test module subclassing jitx.test.TestCase that asserts port counts and per-port membership over list(net) rather than with `in`, and a check entry point that exits nonzero on failure.

assertions.text: the reference connectivity checks pass offline, with no runtime running
the reference design and its checks type-check against the installed JITX package

the candidate's own tests pass, and they subclass jitx.test.TestCase rather than plain unittest.TestCase — outside the JITX instantiation context a design reads as empty and the suite goes green having compared nothing
no bare list is passed to `+=` anywhere in the output — the form raises at instantiation, and on an empty net it raises an unhashable-type TypeError that names neither the call nor the fix
membership is asserted over list(net), never with `in` against the net directly: Net.__contains__ stops at the first nested net, so a port after it reports False while iteration finds it
port COUNTS are asserted, not only membership — 30 on the ground net and 9 on the core net. A membership check alone cannot see a rail that lost half its balls

both ground rails reach one net. Tying GND and leaving RSVDGND floating is the failure this case exists to catch, and it type-checks, builds, and passes any test that only asserts membership of the ports it did tie
the two nets are asserted NOT to be shorted to each other, not merely asserted to contain what they should
every net expression is stored on self. An unstored `a + b` is a discarded connection and nothing downstream reports it
